content.intro: Learn cache backends through a compact visual, an inspectable Django example, and a practical verification task.
content.why_it_matters: Cache Backends matters because a Django project has to behave predictably across requests, database state, configuration, and deployments. Understanding this piece makes the surrounding application easier to test, maintain, and secure.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: This lesson examines cache backends as part of performance, caching, and scalability. The objective is to understand the behavior, connect it to the listed subtopics, and verify it with a small example rather than relying on memorized syntax.

content_blocks.title: What to cover
content_blocks.text: The source syllabus for this lesson names: Local-memory cache; File-based cache; Database cache; Memcached; Redis. Keep these distinct concepts together: know what each item does, when it applies, and what assumption must be verified in your project.

items.title: Local-memory cache
items.text: Cache invalidation and key scope are part of correctness. Include relevant variation dimensions, use a deliberate TTL, avoid cross-user leakage, and invalidate or refresh entries after writes.

content_blocks.title: Worked example: Cache Backends
content_blocks.code:
from django.core.cache import cache

cache.set("public:catalog-summary:v1", {"count": 12}, timeout=60)
summary = cache.get("public:catalog-summary:v1")
content_blocks.expected_output: The example caches a synthetic shared aggregate with an explicit TTL.
